caption: ‘They pierced my hands and feet’ follows a genuinely ancient—but disputed—reading. Even ‘dug’ does not clearly predict crucifixion, and John explicitly quotes Zechariah.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: Did Psalm 22 predict pierced hands and feet? Some ancient texts say the sufferer’s hands and feet were ‘dug’ or ‘pierced.’ Jesus later shows wounds in his hands.
slides.body: Some ancient texts say the sufferer’s hands and feet were ‘dug’ or ‘pierced.’ Jesus later shows wounds in his hands.
slides.heading: Did Psalm 22 predict pierced hands and feet?

slides.alt_text: The BSB text of Ps 22:16: They have pierced my hands and feet.

slides.alt_text: The claimed New Testament fulfilment in Jn 19:34–37, BSB: One of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear … ‘They will look on the One they have pierced.’
slides.body: One of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear … ‘They will look on the One they have pierced.’

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: The reading is genuinely ancient It was not invented by modern Christians. An early Greek translation—and perhaps an early Hebrew copy—supports a verb here.

slides.alt_text: Editorial slide: But the wording is disputed Other Hebrew texts say ‘like a lion.’ Even ‘dug’ does not clearly mean crucified, while John explicitly quotes Zechariah.
